title: Compliance webhook contract for residency + retention events
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers need reliable, machine-readable evidence that artifacts (audit logs, stored request/response blobs, and derived evidence bundles) are created, moved, or deleted with clear residency and retention metadata. We must provide a webhook-based delivery mechanism that carries residency annotations, retention-change events, and packaged evidence references, while meeting enterprise requirements for signing, encryption, replayability, and predictable delivery semantics.

Scope: Define an official webhook event contract and delivery semantics for the following event classes: 'evidence.created', 'evidence.moved', 'evidence.retention.updated', 'evidence.deleted', 'audit.log.appended', and 'evidence.export.requested'. Each event must include: (1) canonical residency tag (region and data residency policy), (2) retention policy reference and effective TTL, (3) evidence bundle reference (signed manifest + presigned URL or storage locator), (4) idempotency key + event sequence id, (5) schema version and human-readable changelog link.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement the webhook delivery infrastructure (retries, DLQ, multi-region routing) but will outline required headers and response codes for compatibility with the infra work owned by ENG-27654. It also does not design the UI in Console for managing subscriber endpoints (a separate PM/Design ticket will cover that).
acceptance_criteria: A fully documented event schema (OpenAPI + JSON Schema) exists for each event class and is stored on Confluence and in repo under /docs/compliance/webhooks
Webhook headers and signature format are defined (HMAC-SHA256 with per-customer key + timestamp + sequence number) and pass a security review
Event payloads include residency and retention metadata fields that map to existing backend enums (region_code, residency_policy_id, retention_tier, ttl_seconds)

Delivery semantics documented: idempotent consumer handling, suggested response codes (200/2xx ack, 429 for rate limit with Retry-After, 5xx for transient failures), and maximum in-flight retries before DLQ
Compatibility tests: end-to-end replay test with a test subscriber in staging proves at-least-once delivery and idempotent processing using provided sample consumer code
Automated generation of a signed evidence manifest for evidence.created events is implemented in the evidence service (spec link provided)
comments: 2025-02-18 Maya Chen: Created ticket after compliance workshop. Initial scope and event classes proposed. Linked to legal requirements doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COM/Residency+and+Retention+Requirements
2025-02-20 Alejandro Ruiz: Drafted initial JSON Schema and pushed examples to GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compliance-specs/pull/212. Needs review from security and infra teams.

2025-02-24 Security review (Inga Patel): Raised concern about replay window and sequence exhaustion; requested sequence rollover policy and per-tenant monotonic counters. Also requested that signing keys be rotated with a KID header and support for JWK discovery endpoint.

2025-02-26 Alejandro Ruiz: Updated schema to include 'sequence_id' (monotonic per-subscriber), 'event_id' (uuid), and 'kid' header. Added guidance for consumer idempotency using event_id. Updated draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compliance-specs/pull/212/commits/4e1a

2025-03-01 Maya Chen: PM review: Added acceptance criteria for retention-update semantics (effective_time vs policy_change_time) and customer-facing contract describing when retention changes take effect for derived evidence. Filed follow-up PM ticket PM-488 for Console UI to display retention-change timeline.

2025-03-03 Alejandro Ruiz: Ran integration test in staging with test-subscriber 'residency-listener-staging'. Observed duplicate events when retry backoff is aggressive; documented recommended backoff (exponential with jitter) and consumer guidance in the spec. Filed infra bug ENG-34210 for broker retry configuration.

2025-03-04 Alejandro Ruiz: Prepared rollout plan: versioned schema v1.0, 30-day dual-write window where both old and new event formats are emitted for customers who register 'schema_version: v1' in subscription. Plan doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COM/Webhook+Rollout+Plan
